title: SW pull failure
sourceDocs: DTP TS tickets via Glean, Jul–Oct 2026

options.label: Right away, within about a minute
Says failed, but it may still be running
options.issue: shows failed but may still be running

options.label: The truck isn't on the office network

howto: Open the VO ticket for this mission in [Jira](https://jira.int.aurora.tech/) (the VO number you were dispatched on).

Find the Shipyard build info field. It must not be blank. Real values from tickets that worked look like one of these: a release label link such as https://go/driver-label/driver-latest-citest, a Shipyard release link ending in something like /shipyard/release/DriverReleaseGroup/20261014_76, or for driver release dev tests a git SHA written as adswpn:// followed by 40 letters and numbers. A bare word, a half-pasted link, or a SHA without adswpn:// in front is a red flag.

Find the Atlas view field. It should name the route you're running, for example dfw_hou. Compare it character for character with a ticket for the same route that pulled fine. One past failure was a missing colon at the end: dal_hou where the working ticket had dal_hou:

Check the goal list name. Open the [Active Goal Lists page](https://confluence.int.aurora.tech/spaces/MOps/pages/893946265/Active+Goal+Lists) in Confluence and find your route. The first column is the Goal List Name and the second is the Display Name. The ticket needs the Goal List Name, for example HOU2_STAGING_1. Scout shows the Display Name, HOU2TerminalStagingLaunch1, so don't copy what you see on screen.

In Scout, look in the bottom right for View update log or View error log and read the error. 'MissionSpec is missing shipyard_build_info field' means the Shipyard field is blank. 'platform_atlas_name ... does not match any in release' means the Atlas view is wrong.
You can't edit these fields yourself. Tell Dispatch or the requestor which field is wrong and what the error said, then pull again once they fix it.
sp_ticket.text: Check the VO ticket's software and route fields
steps: Open the [VO ticket](https://jira.int.aurora.tech/) for this mission.
Confirm it has a Shipyard release or build in the expected format.
Confirm the Atlas view and goal list fields match the route exactly (format matters).
If something is missing or wrong, dispatch or the ticket owner has to fix it. Note what you found.
sp_ticket.help: Most fast failures in past tickets were ticket setup problems, not the truck.

sp_still.text: Let it finish before pulling again
steps: Don't start another pull yet.
Give it a few minutes and re-check the deploy status.
sp_still.help: Scout has shown 'SW Pull Failed' while the deploy kept running and then finished.

sp_long.text: Does it say to reach out to technical support?
sp_long.help: Long installs that timed out returned DEPLOY_FAILED_GET_TECHNICAL_SUPPORT. One GRPC failure at 31 minutes was cleared by a cold start and re-pull.

sp_cs.text: Cold start and retry the pull
steps: TODO: platform cold-start sequence from SOP.
Wait for the truck to reconnect to the tool before doing anything else.
Start the software pull again.
Apply parking brake.
Note: You no longer need to be in the idle stack to cold start. You only need to be in idle when removing logging disks.
Press and hold the Compute Power Button for 5 seconds. PWR indicators blink red.
Wait for both PWR indicators to slow-blink green.
Press and hold the Engine Start Button to turn off the vehicle.
Turn the primary battery bank switch OFF.
Turn the redundant (secondary) battery bank switch OFF.
Ensure both TMS LEDs are off. If on, cycle the battery switches again.
Wait a minimum of 3 minutes.
Ensure the DBW Disconnect is in the up/released position.
Turn the redundant (secondary) battery bank switch ON.
Connect shore power if needed.
Turn the primary battery bank switch ON.
Shore power only: press Engine Start twice. Vehicle power: hold the Engine Start Button.
Ensure both TMS LEDs show amber or green.
Press the drive height recall button.
Press the Compute Power Button for 1 second. It fast-blinks green, then goes steady.
If it takes more than 10 minutes to boot, consult VRE.
Swap to AV stack via TAPP or Scout.
Wait for the truck to reconnect to the tool before doing anything else.
Perform System Shut Down.
Apply parking brake and place transmission in Neutral.
Note: You no longer need to be in the idle stack to cold start. You only need to be in idle when removing logging disks.
Turn ignition key OFF. The LED stays solid green for about 150 seconds, flashes red for about 10 seconds, then turns off.
Wait a minimum of 3 minutes after the LED is off.
Perform System Start Up.
Ensure the DBW Cutoff Switch is in the up/released position.
Engine power: start the engine and keep the ignition key in ON.
Shore power: confirm the shore power switch is off, connect shore power to the vehicle DC receptacle, turn the shore power switch on, then turn the ignition key to ON.
Ensure the Compute Power Button is flashing once per second (system ready to boot).
Press and release the Compute Power Button. The LED fast-blinks green, then burns steadily.
Swap to AV stack via TAPP or Scout.
Wait for the truck to reconnect to the tool before doing anything else.
Perform System Shut Down.
Apply parking brake and place transmission in Neutral.
Note: You no longer need to be in the idle stack to cold start. You only need to be in idle when removing logging disks.
Turn ignition key OFF.
If on shore power: turn the shore power unit switch OFF and disconnect shore power from the vehicle.
Wait a minimum of 2 minutes.
Perform System Start Up.
Press the DBW Disconnect switch.
Start the engine. If on shore power: plug in shore power and turn the key to ON for 5 seconds.
Immediately release the DBW Disconnect button and ensure it is in the up/released position.
Wait for both PWR indicators on the LSI to slow-blink green.
Press the Compute Power Button for 1 second. PWR indicators fast-blink green, then burn steadily.
If the system takes more than 10 minutes to boot, consult VRE.
FG2.1 only: perform the TBS check.
Swap to AV stack via TAPP or Scout.
Wait for the truck to reconnect to the tool before doing anything else.

sp_cs.help: A pull that died late with a communication error re-pulled fine after a cold start (DTP-112058).

steps: Start the software pull one more time.

details: Screenshot: the pull or deploy error, plus the Shipyard release and Atlas view fields on the VO ticket.
sp_esc.text: Operator-level SW pull steps are used up. Open a TS ticket and paste the handoff.
sp_esc.handoffNote: Past causes: VO ticket missing or misformatted Shipyard release / Atlas view (dispatch fix); deploy timeouts or GRPC errors (cold start + re-pull); Scout showing failed while the deploy was still running.

howto: Open the [VO ticket](https://jira.int.aurora.tech/) in Jira and find the Shipyard Build Info field. If you can't see that field at all, no build was specified. That's your problem, so skip to step 6.
Tap the link in that field. It should open the release in Shipyard.

Open [Package Tracker](https://packagetracker.use1-offboard-prod01.ob.cloud.aurora.tech/) and search with the VO number and your truck ID. Always enter the truck ID. Without one it shows "Deployment is Not Ready" even when the build is fine.
Read the result. Ready to deploy means go ahead and pull. Still building means wait and check again. Build failed means the pull will fail too.
If the simulation results are missing, don't pull. Check with Dispatch first.
You can't fix a build yourself. Tell Dispatch or the requestor what Package Tracker showed.
sp_build.text: Check a build is present and the ticket is deployable
steps: Check the Shipyard info to make sure a build is present.
Check [Package Tracker](https://packagetracker.use1-offboard-prod01.ob.cloud.aurora.tech/) to make sure the ticket is deployable.
If the build isn't deployable, work with the requestor to resolve the software build issue before pulling again.
sp_build.source: Dev Ops Troubleshooting Guide v2.2 (Oct 21, 2026), Deploy Issues
sp_build.help: For when Scout shows the SW pull FAILED.

sp_net.text: Try another ethernet cord or port, then cold start
steps: Try a different ethernet cord or a different port.
If that doesn't get you on the network, cold start.
Retry the pull.
sp_net.source: Dev Ops Troubleshooting Guide v2.2 (Oct 21, 2026), NOT on Office Network
sp_net.help: If you still can't get an ethernet connection, it's most likely a hardware issue on the vehicle or on the ethernet port itself.

sp_ota.text: Last resort: pull over the air (cellular)
steps: Start the software pull over the air (cellular) instead of ethernet.
Let it finish before doing anything else.
sp_ota.source: Dev Ops Troubleshooting Guide v2.2 (Oct 21, 2026), NOT on Office Network
sp_ota.help: The guide lists an OTA (cellular) pull as the last resort when ethernet can't be made to work.

sp_forvis.text: Software pull working again without VRE. Post a /vreforvis with the steps you took, a sysreport if possible, and how long you spent troubleshooting.
sp_forvis.source: Dev Ops Troubleshooting Guide v2.2 (Oct 21, 2026), Purpose
